args.summary: The v5.1.0 deployment this morning left payments-api unhealthy with an ~18% error rate across all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west). Rolled back all production regions to the last known-healthy version, v5.0.0. Recommend investigating the v5.1.0 changes before attempting a fix-forward redeploy.
args.title: payments-api degraded after v5.1.0 deploy — rolled back to v5.0.0

trace.final:
Done — payments-api is healthy again. Here's what happened:

1. **Identified the service**: "payments" wasn't a registered service name; the payments service is `payments-api`, which was on **v5.1.0**, unhealthy with an **18% error rate** across all three production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west).

2. **Rolled back**: The deployment history showed **v5.0.0** as the most recent release that was healthy in production (v5.1.0 was marked degraded). I rolled all production regions back to v5.0.0, which succeeded.

3. **Opened a SEV2 incident**: **INC-0001** — "payments-api degraded after v5.1.0 deploy — rolled back to v5.0.0". The on-call engineer has been paged, with full context on the failure and the remediation taken.

4. **Verified recovery**: `payments-api` is now healthy on v5.0.0 in all regions, with the error rate down from 18% to **0.2%**.

Note: re-deploying v5.1.0 (or a fix-forward) would need change-manager approval since v5.1.0 has never been healthy in production — the on-call team should investigate the root cause first.
